data.name: VR Escape The Space Station
data.detailed_description:
In this room escaping VR Game you will become an astronaut who have to escape from a monstrous spaceship. The puzzles within every scene are extremely challenging, be aware of those cabinets and draws, some of them may be hiding secrets.
Pay attention to the minor details of every object as there may be important clues in there, those clues can be crucial for you to un-puzzle the mysteries.
The Game can be played in any space, but you can get the maximum expierence in a room size lager than 3m(length)x2.5m(width)x2.4m (height) .

Instructions:

Press Trigger to grab objects.
Press TouchPad to teleport.

data.short_description: You are trapped in the space station all by yourself. Need to find a way to get the hell out of there. Experience with HTC Vive, consists of 4 rooms full of puzzles. Every scene are elaborately designed including spaceship with zero gravity, outer space landscape corridor and all.

reviews.review:
VR Escape The Space Station is a compact virtual reality puzzle adventure that captures the experimental spirit of early room-scale VR. Instead of relying on action, combat, or elaborate storytelling, it places the player aboard an unfamiliar spacecraft and makes observation the primary tool for survival. You are an astronaut trapped inside the station, and escaping requires exploring your surroundings, discovering hidden clues, manipulating objects, and understanding how seemingly unrelated pieces of information connect. Developed and published by weyha.com, the game originally arrived during the early years of consumer VR, and that heritage is apparent throughout its design.

The adventure is divided across four puzzle-oriented rooms. That may sound modest, but each area is constructed around environmental investigation rather than simply moving from one location to another. Cabinets, drawers, equipment, symbols, and ordinary-looking objects can contain information needed to progress. The result is an experience that encourages patience and careful observation. Sometimes the solution becomes obvious after finding the correct clue, while other puzzles require considerably more experimentation. The satisfaction comes from finally recognizing a connection that may have been sitting in plain sight for several minutes.

Virtual reality gives these familiar escape-room mechanics additional personality. Searching a spacecraft feels more involved when you can physically turn around, examine objects from different angles, and reach toward items using tracked controllers. Interaction is relatively simple, with controller triggers used for grabbing objects and touchpad-based teleportation handling much of the movement. Teleportation is particularly appropriate for an older VR title because it reduces the amount of artificial continuous movement that can cause motion discomfort. The downside is that these mechanics now feel basic compared with newer VR games featuring sophisticated hand tracking, physics, and locomotion systems.

The science-fiction environment is one of the game's more appealing qualities. Being isolated aboard a spacecraft naturally creates tension even without turning the experience into full horror. Metallic interiors, mysterious equipment, windows looking toward space, and unfamiliar technology complement the puzzle design effectively. A zero-gravity-inspired section also attempts to take advantage of the setting rather than making every room feel like a standard terrestrial escape room wearing a science-fiction skin. The visuals themselves inevitably show their age, but the environment still provides an appropriate backdrop for the game's central mystery.

Room-scale movement is another important part of the original design philosophy. Having enough physical space makes it easier to investigate the environment naturally, while teleportation provides an alternative way of repositioning yourself. This approach reflects the period when the HTC Vive and tracked motion controllers were defining how room-scale VR games should work. Players accustomed to modern VR experiences should therefore expect something much simpler in presentation and interaction. The game's age is most apparent in object handling, environmental detail, and the relatively limited sophistication of its VR mechanics.

Difficulty can be both an advantage and a weakness. The game does not constantly direct players toward solutions, so progress often depends on noticing small environmental details. For people who enjoy challenging escape rooms, this encourages genuine deduction instead of simply following objective markers. For others, getting stuck because of an overlooked clue can become frustrating, particularly within a small environment where repeatedly inspecting the same objects eventually becomes tedious. The limited number of rooms also means that overall value depends heavily on how quickly the player solves each puzzle.

Another notable strength is its broad interface language support, making the experience approachable to players from many regions. It is exclusively a single-player game, which suits the premise of being stranded alone aboard a spacecraft. There are no multiplayer distractions, progression systems, or unnecessary secondary mechanics competing with the puzzles. The entire experience remains focused on environmental exploration and escaping the station.

Steam Deck compatibility is effectively unsupported for normal handheld play because this is a VR-only game requiring SteamVR and compatible virtual reality hardware. A Steam Deck by itself cannot provide the tracked headset and motion-controller setup necessary for the intended experience. Even though Steam Deck can potentially participate in unconventional PC or streaming configurations, this should not be mistaken for native Deck compatibility. Anyone purchasing specifically for ordinary handheld Steam Deck gaming should consider the game unsuitable.

Ultimately, VR Escape The Space Station is best viewed as a small piece of early consumer VR history rather than a modern showcase for the technology. Its four-room structure, environmental puzzles, physical object interaction, teleportation movement, and lonely science-fiction atmosphere provide an enjoyable foundation, especially for players who appreciate traditional escape-room problem solving. Its short scope and dated interaction systems prevent it from reaching greater heights, but the central idea remains entertaining when approached with appropriate expectations. For puzzle enthusiasts with compatible VR equipment who enjoy carefully examining environments and solving clues without excessive guidance, there is still some worthwhile entertainment hidden aboard this station.

Rating: 6/10
